method: Primary repository issue timestamps were verified through GitHub REST. Issues are individual reports, not validated general market demand. Competitor capabilities below are attributed to primary READMEs, not benchmarked. Ranking is a qualitative implementation judgement, not a predicted star count.

candidates.name: QuestionLedger (working name)
candidates.concept: A local editable question notebook for planning rounds: stable question IDs, parent context, explicit facts and prerequisites, pending-fact blockers, recorded answer acknowledgements and automatic review state when declared dependencies change.

criteria.evidenceOfDemand: Three concrete November 8 issues from two reporters describe reused references, premature recommendations and confirmations that bring new evidence. They are untriaged, with zero reactions at observation; this supports a specific problem, not broad proven demand.
criteria.distinctValue: Interactive active-question workflow and deterministic dependency-revision review with a small schema. There is substantial overlap with existing ledgers, ADR tools, planning trees and Scrutable; differentiation is narrow usability and a runnable example.
criteria.easeOfDemo: Open a local HTML app with visibly synthetic starter data. Answer questions, change a fact, observe dependent questions require review, then export JSON and Markdown. No account, API key, paid service or real repository data is needed.
criteria.realisticDiscoverability: Searchable problem statement around planning-question context, pending facts and stale decisions; relevant planning, local-first, developer-tools and architecture-decision-record topics. A visual recorded demo is credible. Organic reach remains uncertain and no outreach is authorized.

evidence.title: grilling - lost context
evidence.summary: Reporter loses question context when follow-up rounds reuse numeric labels; asks for stable hierarchical references and original question context alongside answers.
evidence.verification: GitHub REST issue response via connected GitHub fetch

evidence.title: grilling: a recommendation built on a pending fact gets retracted
evidence.summary: Reporter says three recommendations depended on codebase facts still under investigation and had to be retracted. Requests treating recommendation premises as dependencies and keeping affected recommendations provisional.
evidence.verification: GitHub REST issue response via connected GitHub fetch

evidence.title: grilling: a confirmation that brings new facts is treated as the end of the session
evidence.summary: A confirmation included a repository and previous deliverables that changed settled decisions. Reporter requests a new round when confirmation adds constraints or evidence.
evidence.verification: GitHub REST issue response via connected GitHub fetch

competitors.sourceKind: primary repository README; branch contents read and branch head resolved
competitors.summary: Local Markdown decision, lesson and task ledgers, CLI, Claude lifecycle hooks, portable instruction-based integration, explicit supersede/expire/archive lifecycle and structural doctor checks.
competitors.overlap: Local persistence, decision rationale, statuses, stale lifecycle and agent context are already offered.
competitors.proposedDifference: Focus on active question/answer rounds and revision snapshots of explicitly declared evidence; no claim that a local ledger or stale decision detection is novel.

competitors.sourceKind: primary repository README; branch contents read and branch head resolved
competitors.summary: Claude-oriented MCP server extracts ADRs from sessions, records status, creates typed decision links and shows dependencies. It checks age of accepted records for stale alerts; AI modes may use an API key.
competitors.overlap: ADR generation, decision graph, status lifecycle and stale alerts already exist.
competitors.proposedDifference: Small local interactive question editor with deterministic dependency-revision checks, no generation service; difference is workflow and scope, not a new graph concept.

competitors.sourceKind: primary repository README; branch contents read and branch head resolved
competitors.summary: Docs-as-code ADR knowledge base with CLI creation, Markdown storage, searchable static website, timeline, local preview and CI publishing.
competitors.overlap: Searchable local/static decision presentation and documentation lifecycle are established.
competitors.proposedDifference: Editable active questions with pending evidence and changed-evidence review state. Do not claim first local decision website.

competitors.sourceKind: primary repository README; branch contents read and branch head resolved
competitors.summary: CLI creates numbered Markdown Architecture Decision Records and supports superseding prior records while updating their status.
competitors.overlap: Stable decision references, Markdown records and supersession are established.
competitors.proposedDifference: Operate while questions are still unresolved, keeping question ancestry and explicit evidence-revision acknowledgements.

competitors.sourceKind: primary repository README; branch contents read and branch head resolved
competitors.summary: Text-first decision framework with structured question/evidence ledgers, stable identities, dependency graphs, state transitions, reopen-on-evidence-change guidance and an optional structural conformance validator. Its README says interactive navigators remain optional future work.
competitors.overlap: This is the closest conceptual overlap: questions, evidence, dependencies, reopening and validation are already present.
competitors.proposedDifference: A much smaller immediate interactive tool rather than a broad assurance framework. Do not claim invention of evidence-driven reopening or decision readiness; make purely structural readiness explicit.

competitors.sourceKind: primary repository README; branch contents read and branch head resolved
competitors.summary: Portable planning skill keeps Markdown planning trees, stable creation IDs, open questions, decisions, evidence and handoff history across sessions.
competitors.overlap: Question trees, stable IDs and durable planning context already exist.
competitors.proposedDifference: Editable browser notebook and deterministic revision-based review status with import/export; no provider hook or agent is required.

completeFirstVersion: Stable non-reused question IDs and parent relationships
Validated JSON persistence/import/export and Markdown handoff export
Editable facts with pending/resolved state and explicit revisions
Declared prerequisites and deterministic cycle/reference validation
Acknowledgement snapshots; change to own prompt, referenced fact or prerequisite reopens review
Clear pending/stale/ready state based only on recorded information
Keyboard-usable browser UI with explicit save/export behavior
Runnable synthetic example demonstrating lost-context and changed-fact cases
Meaningful regression tests for transitive invalidation, pending facts, imports, ID stability and rendering
limits: The tool cannot discover undeclared dependencies or verify whether a fact is true.
It does not parse arbitrary conversations or guarantee that a person understood an answer.
Readiness is a structural condition within entered data, not approval to execute code or deploy.
No automatic integration with agent sessions is required for first version.
Do not claim unique invention of decision ledgers, dependency graphs, or stale-decision detection.

candidates.name: Glossary relationship explorer
candidates.concept: Import a Markdown glossary, navigate explicit term mentions and backlinks, inspect isolated terms and export a portable interactive map.

criteria.evidenceOfDemand: One November 8 domain-modeling report says a roughly 100-term glossary lacked relationships and proposes explicitly marked canonical term references.
criteria.distinctValue: Interactive map and backlinks could make large glossaries easier to explore, but Markdown term linking and generated indexes already exist. The original issue may be adequately solved by a prompt-format change.
criteria.easeOfDemo: A synthetic commerce glossary demonstrates links and missing targets immediately; drag-and-drop Markdown keeps setup small.
criteria.realisticDiscoverability: Audience includes domain modeling and documentation authors. It is visually demonstrable but narrower than general planning and already overlaps mature documentation tooling.

evidence.title: domain-modeling: glossaries on large domains come out light on relationships between terms
evidence.summary: Reporter says a roughly 100-term glossary lacks expressed relationships and asks for bold canonical term mentions within definitions.
evidence.verification: GitHub REST issue response via connected GitHub fetch

competitors.sourceKind: primary repository README; branch contents read and branch head resolved
competitors.summary: Markdown CLI already links terms to glossary definitions, creates mention indexes and lists, supports aliases/synonyms, multiple glossaries and watch mode.
competitors.overlap: Automatic term cross-linking and navigation already exist.
competitors.proposedDifference: A local visual map and explicit-reference diagnostics; do not infer relationship semantics merely from bold text.

limits: Explicit mentions are not typed semantic relationships.
One issue is limited evidence, and a source skill fix may remove the immediate pain.

candidates.name: Home Assistant automation what-if explorer
candidates.concept: Compare hypothetical automation triggers/entity states and show selected branches and intended actions without affecting devices.

criteria.evidenceOfDemand: November 8 feature request explicitly asks for side-effect-free scenario comparisons for climate/presence automations. Maintainer closed it as out of scope the same day, highlighting engine semantics.
criteria.distinctValue: A portable standalone scenario UI would lower setup, but real-runtime Automation Test Kit already advertises dry runs, trace inspection and synthetic triggers. Reimplementing template/wait/service semantics would be less trustworthy.
criteria.easeOfDemo: An offline synthetic scenario is attractive, but real value requires faithful Home Assistant behavior or a running instance. A tiny supported subset would need visible unknown outcomes.
criteria.realisticDiscoverability: Home Assistant is an active ecosystem and ha-mcp appears in today's rolling Trending snapshot. Nevertheless, competing real-runtime tooling and high semantic risk make a new independent simulator a poor daily-build choice.

evidence.title: [FEATURE] Provide a side-effect-free automation simulation
evidence.summary: Requester wants hypothetical triggers/states to reveal variables, conditions, branches and planned actions without services or notifications.
evidence.verification: GitHub REST issue response via connected GitHub fetch

evidence.summary: Maintainer rejects hand-reimplementing Home Assistant script semantics in ha-mcp, describes existing condition evaluation and real execution paths, and closes the feature as out of scope.
evidence.verification: GitHub REST comments response via connected GitHub fetch

competitors.sourceKind: primary repository README; branch contents read and branch head resolved
competitors.summary: Home Assistant custom integration/panel advertises real traces, synthetic isolated triggers, variable editing and a dry-run that intercepts service calls, driven by Home Assistant's WebSocket API. Requires Home Assistant 2026.9+.
competitors.overlap: Core requested user-facing simulation and dry-run are already provided by an integration.
competitors.proposedDifference: A portable offline experience would be easier to try but risks inaccurate semantics; insufficient credible benefit for this build.

limits: Do not claim general Home Assistant semantics in a tiny offline implementation.
Do not execute real device actions for a demo.
The primary maintainer comment and competitor README are descriptions, not an independent audit of safety.

headroom.summary: Project memory is keyed by cwd so subdirectories/worktrees split memory. Reporter proposes an opt-in git-common-dir strategy with explicit fallback and migration constraints.
headroom.judgement: Concrete November 8 problem, but most naturally a scoped upstream fix or compatibility helper; a separate repo-identity visualizer has weaker standalone usefulness and discoverability than the chosen interactive notebook.

claudeCodeProcessFanout.judgement: Do not use this creation event as November 8 evidence. Only a separately verified November 8 comment could qualify as November 8 activity.

selectionRationale: QuestionLedger ties three same-day reports to one coherent, testable workflow with an immediately useful local demo. It has a modest defensible presentation and workflow difference, while acknowledging close existing prior art. Selection does not imply unique technology or guaranteed demand/stars.
